summary: AI trading research agent that turns plain-English finance questions into reports, backtests and paper portfolios.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Vibe-Trading is a personal trading agent from HKU. You ask finance questions in plain English and it produces research reports, runnable backtests and paper portfolios. It ships as a CLI, a web app, an API and an MCP server.
sixtySeconds.problem: Testing a trading idea normally means writing backtest code and collecting data. Vibe-Trading lets you describe the strategy and see the results, trades and drawdowns.
whoFor: Developers connecting trading research to AI agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for natural-language backtests, an alpha benchmark zoo, trade journal analysis and an investment committee mode, all traceable to the source data.
requirements: An API key for your chosen model provider (or a local model)

overview: Install the package, run vibe-trading init to pick a model provider, then open the interactive CLI. Ask for a backtest in plain English or run vibe-trading alpha bench to benchmark an alpha library.

The web app runs with Docker Compose at http://localhost:8899 after you set your provider and key in agent/.env. Examples include comparing stocks, reviewing your trade history with /journal and /shadow, and following bull and bear cases to a final report.

You can authorize a supported broker to execute live trades within a mandate you set; your funds stay with the broker. Backtests are research, not a promise of future returns. The project is MIT licensed.

steps.code:

cd Vibe-Trading
